descriptionChirho: A digit of the human hand, used both literally (of physical fingers performing actions) and figuratively (of divine power, 'the finger of God'). Singular and plural forms carry the same core sense — the physical appendage or its metaphorical extension to signify direct personal agency. Multilingual glosses are uniform across number: Spanish 'dedo/dedos,' Arabic 'إِصْبَع/أَصَابِع,' Hindi 'उँगली/उँगलियों,' Korean '손가락/손가락들,' Swahili 'kidole/vidole.' Occurrences include Jesus writing with his finger (John 8:6), the finger of God casting out demons (Luke 11:20), Thomas invited to put his finger into the nail marks (John 20:25, 27), and the Pharisees refusing to lift a finger to help (Matt 23:4; Luke 11:46).
